name: mtg-web
description: Commander/EDH deck builder with an AI copilot. React + FastAPI, deployed on Vercel.

paragraphs: A browser-based Commander/EDH deck builder with an AI copilot — live at mtg-workshop.vercel.app.
Claude (Sonnet primary / Haiku fallback) for AI features → Vercel Python Function. Stateless — no persistent disk.
across devices. Without it, the app runs fully in local mode (decks save to the browser; Export/Import moves them, and share links work either way).
features: Frontend: React 19 + Vite, mobile-first responsive, installable PWA → Vercel.
Backend: FastAPI, Scryfall bulk data + Comprehensive Rules baked in at build time,
Accounts + deck sync (optional): Supabase — email magic-link sign-in, decks synced
Analyze — paste a decklist → WUBRG color distribution, mana viability (land+ramp vs curve
target), mana curve, type/rarity breakdown, total price ("as of" date), legality, Commander bracket (1–5, with game-changer callouts).

whatItDoes.text: A browser-based Commander/EDH deck builder with an AI copilot — live at mtg-workshop.vercel.app.

requirements.text: Accounts + deck sync (optional): Supabase — email magic-link sign-in, decks synced
Settings — magic-link / password sign-in (when Supabase is configured), theme switcher.

The parts that took the most judgment: moving the backend off Render onto Vercel Python Functions, setting cache TTLs against Scryfall's own published headers rather than guessing, metering AI spend against a monthly ceiling in backend/app/usage.py, and the Playwright suite in frontend/e2e/ that runs against a hermetic mock backend so no test needs the network or a live API…
